templates.name: Rectangular Microstrip Patch
templates.description: Most common planar antenna. Low profile, easy to fabricate on PCB. Narrowband but can be enhanced with stacked or U-slot designs.
templates.design_notes: Substrate height affects bandwidth (thicker = wider BW but more surface waves). Lower epsilon_r gives wider BW but larger size. Ground plane should extend at least 6h beyond patch edges.

templates.name: Half-Wave Dipole
templates.description: Fundamental resonant antenna. Omnidirectional in azimuth. Serves as reference for gain measurements.
templates.design_notes: Physical length is approximately 0.48*lambda due to end effects. Thick dipoles have wider bandwidth. Folded dipole provides 4:1 impedance transformation and wider bandwidth.

templates.name: Quarter-Wave Monopole
templates.description: Half of a dipole over a ground plane. Omnidirectional in azimuth. Common for handheld devices and vehicular antennas.
templates.design_notes: Requires a ground plane for proper operation. Infinite ground plane gives 5.15 dBi; finite ground planes reduce gain and tilt the pattern upward. Top loading or inverted-L shape can reduce height.

templates.name: Pyramidal Horn
templates.description: Flared waveguide opening. Wideband, high gain, well-characterized. Standard gain antenna for measurements and calibration.
templates.design_notes: Gain determined by aperture size relative to wavelength. Corrugated horns achieve symmetric patterns and low cross-polarization. Conical horns used for circular polarization with appropriate feed.

templates.name: Yagi-Uda Array
templates.description: Endfire parasitic array. High gain from a simple structure. The workhorse of VHF/UHF communications and television reception.
templates.design_notes: Gain increases roughly 1 dB per doubled number of directors. Very narrow bandwidth; optimize for center frequency. Folded dipole driven element provides better impedance match and wider bandwidth.

templates.name: Axial-Mode Helical
templates.description: Circularly polarized wideband antenna. Simple construction with excellent CP performance. Common for satellite communications and GPS.

design_equations.gain_approx: 10 * log10(15 * N * S * C^2 / lambda0^3) dBi

templates.design_notes: Axial mode requires circumference approximately equal to one wavelength. Number of turns determines gain. Right-hand winding gives RHCP. Ground plane should be at least 0.75*lambda in diameter.

templates.name: Vivaldi / Tapered Slot
templates.description: Ultra-wideband endfire antenna with exponentially tapered slot. Excellent for phased arrays, ground-penetrating radar, and UWB systems.
templates.design_notes: Bandwidth ratio > 10:1 achievable. Exponential taper rate R controls beamwidth. Antipodal Vivaldi avoids balun but has higher cross-polarization. Substrate thickness < 0.03*lambda_mid for best performance.

templates.name: Slot Antenna
templates.description: Complement of a dipole by Babinet's principle. Cut in a ground plane, fed by a transmission line. Low profile and flush-mountable.
templates.design_notes: Radiates on both sides of the ground plane (bidirectional). Cavity backing makes it unidirectional. Babinet impedance: Z_slot * Z_complementary_dipole = eta^2/4. Annular slot gives wider bandwidth.

templates.name: Inverted-F Antenna (IFA)
templates.description: Compact low-profile antenna. Shorted patch variant with feed offset for impedance matching. Dominant in mobile phones and WiFi devices.

design_equations.impedance_control: Feed point position between short and open end

templates.design_notes: Height above ground plane is the main bandwidth driver. Shorting pin/wall provides compact lambda/4 resonance. Feed position controls input impedance. Multi-band operation via multiple branches.

templates.name: Planar Inverted-F Antenna (PIFA)
templates.description: Planar version of IFA with a wider top plate. Very common in smartphones for multi-band cellular. Compact with reasonable bandwidth.

design_equations.height: 5 to 10 mm typical for cellular bands
design_equations.impedance_control: Shorting pin/wall width and feed position

templates.design_notes: Width of shorting wall affects bandwidth (wider = more BW). Top plate dimensions L+W approximately lambda/4. Dual-band via slots in top plate or parasitic elements. SAR reduction compared to external antennas.

templates.name: Archimedean Spiral
templates.description: Frequency-independent antenna with inherent circular polarization. Ultra-wideband with consistent gain across decades of bandwidth.
templates.design_notes: Active region radiates where circumference equals one wavelength. Self-complementary design gives constant 188.5 ohm impedance. Cavity backing makes unidirectional but narrows bandwidth. Absorber-loaded cavity is a compromise.

templates.name: Bowtie (Biconical Dipole)
templates.description: Wideband planar dipole variant. Triangular flare provides broader bandwidth than a linear dipole. Simple and inexpensive to fabricate.
templates.design_notes: Wider flare angle gives wider bandwidth but lower impedance. Printed bowtie on substrate is narrower band than free-space. Resistive loading or rounded edges further improve bandwidth.

templates.name: Loop Antenna
templates.description: Electrically small or resonant loop. Small loops have magnetic dipole pattern. Resonant loops (1-lambda circumference) provide moderate gain.
templates.design_notes: Electrically small loops (circumference < lambda/10) are poor radiators but useful for direction finding and near-field probes. Resonant loops have circumference near one wavelength. Multiple turns with tuning capacitor for HF reception.
